**Total ≈ $6,609 landed** ($5,747 + 15% contingency; target ≤ $4,000 since D9 (owner: sensors over savings); limit $5,500 (owner, 2026-11-27; was $5,000); excludes the owner's Pi 5 and tools). Single-unit online prices; hardware lines are ESTIMATEs.

**Loop 47 cost pass** (motor choices unchanged; before → after, each with the 15 % contingency):
- A5 v2 safety electrics added first: DC contactor with aux contact, switched pre-charge, energy-rated regen clamp: $71 → $208 of lines (+$158 landed): $5,030 → $5,188.
- Savings (−$290 landed): PETG in 10 kg bundles ($333 → $220); five $19 candleLight USB-CAN adapters in place of the CAN HAT + three $35 adapters ($152 → $95); one USB-TTL adapter instead of three (the D14 nodes drive the buses); no separate balance charger (the dock's CC/CV charger + the BMS's active balancing do the weekly 4.20 V charge, A13); GIM6010-8 at the verified $90, DM-J4310 at $150 in stock, RPLIDAR C1 at $69.
- Result: **$4,898**, under the $5,000 limit; the $4,000 target would need the motor or sensor choices reopened.

**Wave 1 (D24 bolted cartridges, D19 one-piece shafts; 2026-11-27): $4,898 → $5,013 landed.** The arm's 10 KX sockets go (balls, dowel packs, springs, torque pins: −$35 of lines); in: 8 Oldham couplings ($96; the spare acetal rod is an M1 bench item), heat-set inserts ($44), flange screws ($10), Ø6 dowels for the yaw stops and ferrules ($6); the D13 flange couplings go (−$24); D14 buck 3 → 6 A (+$4); PETG from the re-sliced print plan. +$13 against the $5,000 limit at the time. The owner's OK for the inline GIM8108-36 roll then put two GIM8108-36 in place of two GIM6010-8 (at the yaml's $171): $5,199.

**Fable review fixes (2026-11-27, M2 + M7): $5,308 → $5,485 landed (+$177).** A third clamp resistor + MOSFET (the inline roll raised the robot's peak regen to 2.8 kW), the safety-board logic the netlist needs (one-shot discharge, latch, comparators), and aluminium finned rear caps + thermistors on the six arm GIM6010 cartridges (a closed ASA sleeve allows only 0.65 × rated continuous). The C1/M1 joint hardware (tie-rods, 6061 yaw flange, 7075 crank) was in the M1 kit only until W10 (below).

**Neon review #2 fixes (2026-11-27; findings 1, 10, 11, 12 and the keyed D50 drive of 2/15): $5,485 → $5,845 landed (+$360).** NH-50 clamp resistors + freewheel Schottkys (+$51), a 200 A BMS for the 40 A class (+$50), a steel battery box (+$20), 60 A main fuse (+$10), XT90 / XT60 / USB pogo connectors (+$12), the lift umbilical (+$30), 16 AWG fluoropolymer ribbon wire (+$10), the dock baseplate and taller pads instead of floor screws (+$14), keyed stages and D50 Oldhams instead of plain shafts and D40s (+$111), the netlist-v3 logic (+$5); plus contingency.

**W10 consolidation of the wave-8 hardware (2026-11-27; W8b cartridge, W8c load path, W8d tip): $5,845 → $7,949 landed (+$2,104), +$2,449 against the $5,500 limit.** The D50 Oldham was a $20 generic ESTIMATE with no source, keyway or torque rating; it is now priced as the parts the cartridge calls for (Ruland MOCC51-12-A keyed clamp hub $67.19 + OD32/51-AT acetal disc $36.45 at Zoro) with a 6061 motor-side hub (the printed ASA tongue was rejected) on all 7 GIM6010 stages (the lift's was missing), 2 spare discs; 4-ear flange screws with nuts replace the countersunk M4s; turned 42CrMo4 crush sleeves at every C1 tie / clevis / rear-mount bolt + 2 stop bushes, the 7075 rear plate, M4 × 25 rear screws and Loctite 660 / 638 (no Belleville springs; the M4 × 18 + shims and the Ø10 stop dowels go); the elbow's 6061 core tube; D18b lockable 2" casters with solenoid release and the 2 × 2.44 kg ballast (W8d's ≈ $80 ESTIMATE was ≈ $410 of lines priced); and the C1 joint hardware (tie-rods, 6061 yaw flange, 7075 crank) that was in the M1 kit only. - Belt-roll parts out (2 Oldham, 2 D13 stages, 2 belts, 4 × 61808, 4 × 6801: −$72); inline parts in (2 × 7075 output adapter at a $30 CNC ESTIMATE, 2 × 61806, steel clamp ring + screws + dowels: +$88). A printed adapter is not an option (3 × M4 into PETG ≈ 85 N·m < 103 N·m stall).
- Sensor nodes 3 → 5 (sw/config/can_map.yaml has a shoulder and an elbow node per arm): +$20.
- Savings: DM-J4310 $150 → **$125** (AIFit Lab, 24 V, US seller, backordered: the full-robot buy comes after M1): −$50; D23 covers $60 → $30 (the rigid covers, 1.4 kg of PETG, fit in the 10 kg bundles: 18.2 kg needed with spare of 20 kg bought; TPU 95A + fasteners stay): −$30.
- Not taken: Foxtech DM-J4310 $116–120 (ships from China: tariff/duty exposure eats the gap); pultruded CF (higher axial E, but the forearm's double-D pinch clamp and 1 mm wall split a unidirectional tube; roll-wrapped listings are already $63–70); DIY 6S2P from cells (≈ −$50, but a home-welded pack without a spot welder or cell matching is a safety risk in a home robot); generic D40 Oldham (no sourced price under $12; Ruland/GMT $36–67); cheaper heat-set inserts (the short M4 is $11–21 / 50 elsewhere); a lower contingency (this pass found a +40 % price on one line, and China-direct parts now pay duty: 15 % stays); Gemini 2 / RPLIDAR C1 / battery / GIM6010-8 are already at the best sourced price.
- **+$1,109 against the $5,500 limit** (owner raised it from $5,000 on 2026-11-27 to keep the inline roll and the review fixes). The belt roll (fallback `PIP_ROLL_DRIVE=belt`) is −$569 landed; the owner chose the inline roll for its hand-feel and slimmer shoulder.
